#2749. Brown puts up 30 as Sixers hang on to avenge lone loss with win over Pistons

It could have been easier, but the Sixers have defeated the Detroit Pistons for the first time since November of 2024, knocking them off 112-106 Wednesday night.

Jaylen Brown set a new season-high 30 points shooting 11-of-19 from the floor, and his biggest play was blocking Cade Cunningham's three-point attempt with 38 seconds remaining. LeBron James came close to his first triple-double as a Sixer, putting up 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists on 5-of-10 shooting.

Tyrese Maxey had his worst shooting performance of the season, put up 17 of his 19 in the second half going 5-of-16 from the floor along with seven assists. Not playing on a minutes restriction this time, Joel Embiid shot 8-of-18 for 26 points and 14 rebounds.

Cunningham led the Pistons with 26, who were once again without Jalen Durn who remains sidelined with a hamstring injury, as well as Isaiah Joe who injured his hip when these two teams last met on Oct. 25.

It was tough sledding early for Embiid and Maxey, each missing their first three field goals of the night despite some good looks. Embiid missed his 12th straight three-pointer dating back four games now, but he was able to help the offense flow in spite of that. He found a cutting Brown for the first points of the game and got his first field goal on a backdoor cut on his own.

Paul Reed had quite a start against his old club. He stayed in front of Maxey on a drive and blocked his layup attempt, and made his first two shots of the night attempting some fancy footwork. Getting one slam called back for a travel didn't sway his confidence in trying to spin around Embiid.

LeBron settled in as he began to run the offense more after the Sixers' first subs. After finding Embiid on that cut, he got aggressive with their pick-and-roll, getting each of them to the free throw line during this stretch. A steal caused by Dean Wade ending in a Dean Wade layup capped off a 10-0 Sixers run.

Brown and Maxey finished the quarter strong as the Sixers flipped the stagger with a couple minutes to go. Maxey's scoop layup were only his first points of the night, but Brown was good in all nine of his minutes. He got the basket off the dribble for an and-1 then became the latest Sixer to hit an end-of-quarter heave, putting the Sixers up eight after one.

They went right back to Brown on their first possession of the quarter and he got right to his spot in the midrange for another jumper. LeBron got an assist for that, but his impressive dimes came on his consecutive assists to Adem Bona. He waited just long enough for Reed to slide over for a quick bounce bass on the first, and the second was a left-handed laser from half court to reward Bona for getting down the floor ahead of the defense.

Cunningham started this game 2-of-8 from the floor. He also got hit in the midsection in the first quarter. Detroit's offense struggled as their head of the snake did and the Sixers were able to take advantage. James got to the basket a couple more times, becoming the first player in history to reach 16,000 career field goals in the process. Brown drilled two more threes to cap off his heater. After intercepting a pass he had a wide open layup to himself but smoked it after an uneasy takeoff. Brown said the other day he's waiting for a bit more burst to come back so hopefully this is just a blip on the radar.

A couple of turnovers to follow up that layup helped the game slowly swing the Pistons' way for the first time. After a cutting layup, Duncan Robinson drilled his third and Detroit's fourth three of the night. Maxey checked back into the game to get the offense back up and running but was subbed right back out after picking up his third foul of the night in just 10 seconds.

Embiid put back a missed layup and drew a foul in the process to end a 9-0 Sixers run, but picked up a technical foul after really getting into with reserve center Tolu Smith. It just seemed like an odd escalation from typical dead ball shooting from both parties.

That foul occurred when Brown was due for two at the line, drilling both to help offset the technical. After forcing a turnover Embiid got himself to the line getting Smith to bite on a rip through. Brown got to the line one more time and split a pair to give the Sixers a 14-point lead at halftime.

The Sixers gave Cunningham too much space as he dribbled around a screen, helping him step into an open three to start the half. He also read an Embiid outlet very well for a pick-six moments later. Edgecombe had answered with a pull-up jumper and a cutting dunk, but as Cunningham started to draw doubles, the Sixers left John Collins wide open for lobs, prompting a timeout from Nick Nurse.

Nurse went back to his hot hand coming out of the timeout and Brown drilled a contested turnaround midrange jumper. LeBron drilled a three off the catch, as did Maxey for just his second field goal of the night on the following possession. Cunningham responded by getting to the line, then taking advantage of a collapsed defense to find Robinson for another three.

As he has all year, Edgecombe was doing a great job filling the lanes and was rewarded with plenty of open dunks for doing so. He also swooped in to grab a missed Embiid layup for a big putback basket. A couple possessions later he grabbed a big rebound on the defensive end and took the ball to the hoop to help the Sixers withstand Robinson's heater.

Maxey checked back in and hit a sidestep three, a much welcomed sight after his first half. Despite the Pistons getting a pair of free throws on the ensuing possession the Sixers got up the floor quickly and found Kentavious Caldwell-Pope in the corner for a three. Brown split another pair at the line and hit another midrange J to set a new season-high for this young season. Despite some good ball pressure that led to a turnover, Edgecombe wasn't able to finish a fastbreak layup, keeping the Sixers at a 16-point lead.

Once again the Sixers started their quarter going to Brown and once again he was able to rise up and knock one down inside the arc. With Embiid having played 24 minutes and Jabari Walker at the scorer's table it wasn't clear if Embiid's night was over, and Detroit was picking up momentum going to the basket. After four possessions ended in three layups, Nurse called a timeout and put Embiid back in the game. Bona didn't just sub out but went to the locker room after taking a hit to the head during his shift.

Kevin Huerter drilled a three coming out of that timeout continuing the pursuit, but Embiid was able to knockdown a jumper to settle things down. Maxey drove his way to the line and LeBron was able to find KCP near the hoop for a basket. They surrendered a fast break that led to another Pistons three, but Reed picking up his fifth foul of the night for a thin Detroit backcourt and Maxey being left alone for another three on the left wing put the Sixers in a good spot with four and a half to go.

After missing a three badly at the end of the shotclock, Maxey appeared to make up for it running out after a miss, but he smoked the fast break layup as well. Brown fouled Robinson attempting a three on the following possession for a big swing.

Robinson made two of the three after a timeout. The Sixers went to the Maxey/Embiid two-man game and a pocket pass set the big fella up for a much needed midrange jumper, but they couldn't keep Robinson down for too long as he buried another three coming off a screen. LeBron had Edgecombe set up for a rolling layup down the lane but Edgecombe fumbled the pass, giving up another easy open basket at the rim for Philadelphia.

Capping off a messy night of officiating, Cunningham got a pair at the line on a play he either should have had an and-1 or the foul be on the floor. Regardless, he cut the lead to six. LeBron followed it with a poor jumper behind the block that didn't go and Cunningham got right back to the basket to cut it to a four-point game.

The Sixers dribbled out their next possession and the ball swung to Embiid behind the perimeter with the shotclock winding down, but he was unable to bust out of his long range slump. It was fitting that Brown made the biggest play of the night, blocking Cunningham's pull-up three-point attempt on the next trip down the floor. It set the Sixers up to win the game from the free throw line and summed up in one play why the Sixers beat the Pistons for the first time in their last eight tries.

The Sixers were able to win the game at the line, but they might have picked up a considerable bump or bruise to worry about. As he was trying to avoid turning the ball over, Maxey came up favoring his right hand as Detroit was fouling him. He's dealt with finger injuries on that hand in each of the last two seasons. Maxey was at least able to hit four straight free throws to help the Sixers pull out the win.

#2748. Eagles should take another chance on young QB to pair with Saquon Barkley

Eagles should take another chance on young QB to pair with Saquon Barkley originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Philadelphia Eagles have had to make some difficult decisions with their quarterback room over the past couple of weeks, unfortunately because of Jalen Hurts' injury.

It remains unclear what the Eagles plan to do over the next couple of days before the NFL trade deadline, but reports indicate Philadelphia is starting Joe Milton against the New York Giants on Sunday.

This will allow the Eagles an opportunity to figure out if they can salvage their season, as the only concern with this team has really been on the offensive side of the football.

The defense hasn't been as great as it typically is, but it's still been better than the offense. If the offense can do what's needed, it should be more than fine. If Milton doesn't play the type of football everybody's hoping for, Philadelphia could still make a trade for a player who hasn't proven a whole lot yet but has a ton of upside.

That guy would be none other than Anthony Richardson. After the Baltimore Ravens traded for Jacoby Brissett, it feels like Richardson's the type of player other teams could be interested in.

CBS recently suggested the Ravens could have moved Richardson before this trade, but with Brissett now getting the job, it's interesting to think about how those same benefits in Baltimore could translate to Philadelphia with Saquon Barkley.

"Anthony Richardson Jr. requested a trade from the Colts earlier this year. #2746. NFL Week 9 Injury Report: Jeremiyah Love hits IR, Lamar Jackson likely done for season, and more

Staying up to date on NFL injury news is of the utmost importance for fantasy football success. The article below tracks all fantasy-relevant players currently listed on their team's injury report and provides fantasy managers with actionable recommendations as new information rolls in.

Check back for updates from Tuesday through Saturday.

**UPDATED AS OF WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 4 AT 8:00 PM ET**

The Bills emerged from their Week 8 win over the Ravens absent any fantasy-relevant injuries.

Impact: Willis practiced in full with the same injury last week before rushing just once on game day. The injury could be limiting him in-game, though he remains a QB2 against the Lions.

Impact: Kayton Allen (quad) was limited. He could end up challenging Wright for the No. 2 role at some point.

Achane suffered a torn ACL in the team's Week 3 loss to the Chiefs, ending his season.

Impact: Achane's unfortunate season-ending injury creates opportunity for Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright. The timing of the injury makes it likely that Achane is able to fully recover before the start of the 2027 regular season.

Hollins departed the team's Week 4 win over the Bills with a calf injury and did not return. He was placed on injured reserve in Week 5. Hollins resumed practicing in Week 9.

Impact: Hollins' potential return clouds the pass-catching corps' Week 9 prospects.

Doubs was placed on injured reserve following a shoulder injury sustained in Week 6. He will miss the next four games, at minimum.

Impact: The Patriots have now played only 33 offensive snaps with both Doubs and A.J. Brown on the field together this season after Doubs was injured on his second offensive snap in Week 6. Brown returned from injured reserve in Week 6 and should have the runway to return WR1 numbers while Doubs remains sidelined.

Brown was limited on Wednesday but downgraded to "DNP" Thursday and Friday, ultimately ruled out for Week 8 against the Dolphins. Brown remains sidelined to begin Week 9.

Impact: DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism stepped up in Brown's absence, but Mack Hollins (calf) could return this week, adding volatility for fantasy purposes.

Henderson was ruled out Saturday with an illness after missing practice Wednesday and Thursday. He remains sidelined to begin Week 9.

Impact: Rhamondre Stevenson should operate as a clear workhorse for as long as Henderson remains sidelined, while Corey Kiner is in line to serve as the primary change-of-pace option.

Henry left early in Week 8 after injuring his foot. He did not practice the following Wednesday.

Impact: Eli Raridon vaults into the streaming TE1 tier.

Hall has missed the previous five games but is tentatively expected to return in Week 9 against the Chiefs. However, he remains limited to begin Week 9.

Impact: Braelon Allen may have earned himself a weekly rushing role during Hall's absence, though we will not know for sure until this week's game transpires. If both players are active, Hall is a high-end RB2. Allen is flex-viable.

Impact: Taylor should face the Chiefs this weekend, though he is only a TE2/3.

Jackson returned from an ankle injury in Week 8 and made it all of one offensive snap before suffering a thumb injury that is likely to sideline him for the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Jackson's absence is the biggest hit to the fantasy value of alpha receiver Zay Flowers, who falls to a mid-range WR2 in rest of season rankings.

Huntley suffered a season-ending turf toe injury in the team's Week 8 loss to the Bills. Impact: The Ravens suddenly find themselves in scramble mode to save a sinking season, with both Lamar Jackson and Huntley expected to miss significant time, the former of whom appears to be done for the season. Rookie Joe Fagnano came on in relief against the Bills and could not sustain drives, leaving the team in dire need of consistent quarterback play. Fagnano is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury and was seen wearing an ankle guard/brace in practice Tuesday. Fagnano will start on Thursday night, though the Ravens are expected to start trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett in Week 10. The Jaguars D/ST is an elite play in Week 9.

The Ravens activated Randall's 21-day practice window on Wednesday. He is questionable for Week 9.

Impact: Justice Hill (groin) will play. Randall can be stashed in deep leagues.

Smythe suffered a torn Achilles in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans. His season is done.

Impact: It was Matt Hibner who saw the largest increase in snaps following Smythe's departure in Week 4, making it unlikely we see veteran Mark Andrews in a more robust role.

The Bengals placed Iosivas on injured reserve in Week 3

Impact: Wide receivers Colbie Young and Dohnte Meyers will duke it out for the No. 3 wide receiver role for at least the next four weeks. Meyers can be added in 14-team leagues, though his upside is questionable.

All suffered a torn ACL in Week 7. He was placed on injured reserve Tuesday and will miss the remainder of the regular season.

His absence could provide a slight uptick in snap rate and route participation for Mike Gesicki, although he will be a difficult weekly start for as long as both Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain healthy.

Watson suffered a concussion in Week 8 and was sidelined the following Wednesday.

Wilson departed in the second half of Week 5 with a finger injury and is reportedly looking at a multi-game absence. He was ruled out for Week 6 on Friday and placed on injured reserve on Saturday.

Noel suffered a turf toe injury in Week 7. The Texans placed him on injured reserve in Week 8. He is expected to miss the remainder of the regular season.

Impact: Tank Dell and recent acquisition Marvin Harrison Jr. would be in line to benefit. Harrison should be added in 12-team formats.

The Texans placed Jordan on injured reserve in Week 7.

Impact: Jordan prevented Marks from handling a full-time role in Week 6. Dare Ogunbowale will probably do the same while Montgomery is sidelined.

Higgins saw his 2026 season taken from him due to a torn ACL suffered in camp.

Tuten did not practice at all this week. He is questionable to play and coach Liam Coen said he will be a game-time decision.

Impact: The Ravens are forced to start their injured QB3 on Thursday night. The Jaguars run the ball whenever possible. If Tuten is active, he is an RB1. If Tuten sits, Rodriguez vaults into the RB2 tier.

Rodriguez will play on Thursday night. Impact: See above.

Meyers is cleared to play on Thursday night.

Thornton suffered a devastating ankle injury due to a hip-drop tackle in Week 4. He is reportedly set to undergo surgery within the week and will miss 12-16 weeks.

Impact: The return of Rashee Rice left little volume for the secondary options through the air in Week 8, a setup that appears likely to continue forward for the Chiefs.

The Raiders emerged from their Week 8 win over the Jets absent any fantasy-relevant injuries.

Njoku is reportedly set to see his 21-day practice window opened in the coming days. He was limited to begin Week 9.

Ferguson departed the team's Week 8 loss to the Cardinals with an ankle injury in the first quarter and did not return. He sat out on Wednesday.

Pickens is no longer listed with a shoulder injury. He was limited on Wednesday.

#2745. Dianna Russini gets out the word that she's coming back to work next week

The halfway point of the 2026 NFL season arrives this weekend. Next week, Dianna Russini apparently will return to sports media.

Per a source with knowledge of the situation, Russini has begun getting the word out to people in the league that she’ll be returning to work “next week.”

It’s unclear where she’ll be working, or what she’ll be doing.

She resigned from The Athletic in April, one week after photos were published by the New York Post of Russini and Patriots coach Mike Vrabel at a resort in Arizona. In both her comments to the Post and her resignation letter to The Athletic, she denied that there was any type of impropriety.

The Athletic conducted a review of her work. Its findings were released in early September.

“Russini’s relationship with Vrabel was in clear violation of The Athletic’s standards,” wrote Mike Semel of The Athletic, who conducted the investigation. “Regardless of whether the relationship was romantic, it was a breach and should have been disclosed.”

Beyond the relationship was the manner in which she handled the emergence of the controversy.

"[W]hen first confronted with the photos by The New York Post,” Semel wrote, “Russini waited two days before telling her editors and managers. She then told a story to explain the photos that did not align with facts, raising issues of trust.”

Along the way, a strange story emerged regarding Russini being pulled over for texting while driving — made stranger by her decision to tell the story publicly and embellish the notion that she FaceTimed a head coach for help in getting out of the ticket.

So if she’ll be reporting again, she’ll need to restore her own credibility. Especially given the unique set of facts that resulted in her departure from The Athletic.

#2744. Celtics survive late stampede from Bucks, win 109-102

The Celtics led the Bucks by as many as 22 points on Wednesday night before the Bucks made a big comeback and briefly took the lead in the fourth. Thankfully for Boston, Paul George and Derrick White saved the day as the Celtics held on with a 109-102 win.

Jayson Tatum did not play in this game for the Celtics and Boston started Derrick White, Sam Hauser, Paul George, Hugo Gonzalez and Neemias Queta. Devin Carter was still out with mono as well. Meanwhile, the Bucks started Tyler Herro, Brayden Burries, Kyle Kuzma, Jaine Jacquez Jr. and Myles Turner and were only missing two-way player Kam Jones.

The Celtics got off to a quick start, going up 19-8 mid way through the first quarter. After Sam Hauser hit the first two shots of the game, Paul George scored 7 of the next 13 Celtics points.

The Celtics led after the first quarter 28-14. Paul George led the way with 10 points and 3 steals while playing the entire quarter. Mitchell Robinson also had 6 rebounds off of the bench.

Boston got off to a good start in the 2nd quarter as Payton Pritchard had a few baskets. It was good to see Payton Pritchard be aggressive on his first shot as well. However, a pair of Bucks threes leading to a 6-2 run lead to Joe Mazzulla calling his mandatory timeout.

The offense picked up in the 2nd quarter, as Boston led 62-41 at the half. Luka Garza led the way with 11 points and 5 rebounds while Derrick White had 9 points, 4 assists and 3 rebounds.

It was good to see the Celtics three point shooting get going, they were 10/17 in the first half after being 30% in their last 4 games, according to the NBC Sports Boston broadcast.

Boston came out flat in the 2nd half and Milwaukee took advantage. The Bucks went on a 12-5 run to open the 3rd quarter and Joe Mazzulla called a timeout. Jamie Jaquez Jr. had 5 points and Tyler Herro had 4 points during the run for Milwaukee.

The Bucks made 10 of their first 12 shots in the quarter and cut the Celtics led to 7. Back-to-back key Baylor Scheierman threes grew Boston's lead back to 13 as Milwaukee called timeout.

Payton Pritchard left the game with an right eye abrasion and he did not return to the game.

It was Tyler Herro's quarter, he had 17 points on 6/8 from the field and 2/2 from three in the 3rd quarter.

The Celtics did lead the Bucks at the end of three but what was a 21-point game at halftime was just an 8-point lead entering the fourth. Paul George's 16 points, 4 assists and 2 steals led the way for Boston.

The Bucks opened the fourth quarter on a 10-4 run and forced Joe Mazzulla to call another timeout.

Milwaukee took their first lead with 6:50 to go in the game but Boston fought back and took a 3 point lead as Taylor Jenkins called timeout.

The Celtics struggled score as they missed Tatum and Pritchard a lot. It felt like Paul George was their only source of offense late in the game.

George then stepped up to the line with under 4 minutes left and missed both free throws in a tie game.

The Celtics were able to go on a 7-0 run thank to 5 points from Derrick White to take a 104-97 lead, which Tyler Herro cut to 104-99 with two made free throws.

Paul George hit a clutch 3 to put the Celtics up 8, Ryan Rollins hit a 3 and the Bucks had a few looks to cut the Celtics lead to 2 with just over 30 seconds to go but they missed both.

Two Derrick White free throws iced it and the Celtics hung on, 109-102. George's 25 points and White's 24 points led the way for the Celtics.

Boston shot 41% from the field and 41% from three while Milwaukee shot 41% from the field and 40% from three. The Celtics next game is an NBA Cup game in Charlotte at 7 pm EST on Friday night.

#2741. Ravens trading for Jacoby Brissett helps 49ers keep Mac Jones in San Francisco

Ravens trading for Jacoby Brissett helps 49ers keep Mac Jones in San Francisco originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

It always felt like if the San Francisco 49ers were going to move on from Mac Jones, it would take a massive trade haul to get the deal done.

Not that Jones is one of the best quarterbacks in the world by any measure, but there's reason to believe he can come into a team dealing with a quarterback issue and help them succeed.

One of the more obvious teams in the league that could have used a player like Jones was the Baltimore Ravens, though it's now been reported that Baltimore is making a trade for Jacoby Brissett with the Arizona Cardinals.

Before this trade, one CBS writer floated the idea that the Ravens could be interested in trading for Jones, and that, for that to happen, they'd have to blow away the 49ers in a potential trade.

"It doesn't seem particularly realistic. Kyle Shanahan has said many times he wants to keep Jones, and the 49ers, like the Bears, have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations right here, right now. If the 49ers needed a spot start — or even just a few series — from Jones to win a game, it would be worth it. Unlike the Bears, though, the 49ers don't have a second legit backup. Kurtis Rourke has never played an NFL snap.

"The Ravens would likely need to blow away the 49ers to have any shot at Jones, and that simply hasn't been Baltimore GM Eric DeCosta's M.O. Instead, Bagent and Brissett seem like top options, with a flyer on a younger, potentially intriguing player also a legitimate route for the Ravens to take," CBS' Zachary Pereles wrote.

While this doesn't guarantee the 49ers won't move on from Jones, it does raise the question of which other team in the league would be interested in taking a decent-sized haul to save their season.

With Baltimore now likely out of the mix, that's one other team the 49ers can't use as leverage. The 49ers still have about a week before they need to decide on Jones, though it seems obvious now that he isn't going to get traded, barring something drastic happening.

#2737. Kellen Moore confirms Charlie Smyth will kick for the Saints this week

The Saints released veteran kicker Daniel Carlson on Tuesday. Coach Kellen Moore confirmed Wednesday that Charlie Smyth will kick for them this week.

“Yeah, Charlie will kick this week,” Moore said, via video from the team. “Tough decisions. Daniel, he’s made some really good kicks for us. I think just the consistency thing. Smyth, a native of Northern Ireland, went 12-of-16 on field goals in six games for the Saints in 2025.

#2735. Jalen Brunson's 22 first-quarter points kickstart Knicks' 135-105 smackdown of Bulls

The Knicks took advantage of a floundering Chicago Bulls defense -- ranked 29th of 30 in the league -- Wednesday night, winning their third-straight game and their fourth in the last five with a final score of 135-105.

-- New York came out of the gate fast, stunning a young Bulls team into a state of near paralysis. Chicago surrendered 10 points off of turnovers through the first 13 minutes of play, while the Knicks, who have struggled in transition so far this season, let up none across the same span. The Bulls also faltered from beyond the arc, missing 20-straight threes in the middle stretch of the first half. Led by Jalen Brunson's 26 first-half points, New York went into the break with a dominating 32-point lead (84-53).

-- After struggling to find the basket through the first few games of the season -- and missing his first three of Wednesday's game -- Brunson looked back to peak form in the first quarter, scoring a staggering 22 points in 11 first-quarter minutes. Collectively, the Bulls only scored 21 in the opening frame.

Even with significantly decreased minutes in the back half of the contest, Brunson continued to produce, finishing the night with 33 points, two rebounds, and four assists.

-- The Knicks went 24-for-26 from the charity stripe in the first half. OG Anunoby contributed nearly half of those points.

He drew 10 free throws in the first 14 minutes of play -- marking the second-straight game in which he earned eight attempts -- and landed every one for 10 of his 18 first-half points. A third personal foul with 8:48 left in the opening half stifled his run as he sat for the next five minutes, and while he drew two more foul shots before the half wound down, he only hit one. Still, his 11 made free throws tied a career-best mark for most in the first half.

-- Karl-Anthony Towns finished the game with his eighth-consecutive double-double (17 points, 12 rebounds), completing the set less than halfway through the third despite only recording one shot from the field by the end of the first half. He opened the third quarter with two back-to-back threes and only turned up the heat from there.

Toward the end of the second frame, Towns jumped up to shoot a three but was met by Chicago forward Zach Collins, who knocked the ball out of Towns' hand. On his way down, Collins stepped on Towns' toe and knocked him over, triggering a review for a flagrant foul. However, because Collins' foot landed on top of Towns' rather than below, the move was ruled as a common foul instead, and Towns earned three free throws. He made all three.

-- With Josh Hart sidelined due to ankle soreness, Landry Shamet joined New York's starting five for the first time this season. The shooting guard more than earned the right Monday, lifting the Knicks to a win against the Brooklyn Nets with a game-leading 22 points.

-- For the second game in a row -- and third in the last week -- New York's bench combined for 40-plus points (53 on Wednesday). This time, Jordan Clarkson and Dalton Knecht led the way.

His second -- a 25-foot step-back jump shot -- put the Knicks at 84 first-half points, tying the franchise record for most points scored in the opening 24 minutes of a game. He also added seven rebounds and an assist.

Clarkson, who also scored 10, went 4-for-9 from the field and 2-for-2 from three.

Mohammed Diawara, who first subbed in for Anunoby with five minutes left in the first, collected three points, one rebound, and one block in three first-quarter minutes. He finished with eight points, tied with James Wiseman for second-most on the bench.

Late in the third, Miles McBride leapt up for a 24-foot jumper from deep at the play clock buzzer before he was knocked over, drawing a foul and turning the sequence into a four-point play. He finished with seven points.

-- All 14 available Knicks made an appearance. Everyone except Jose Alvarado and Pacome Dadiet played 11 minutes or more. They each played nine.

The star point guard finished 10-for-17 from the field, 5-for-10 from three-point range, and 8-for-9 from the free throw line en route to a season-best 33-point performance. No other Knick surpassed 18 points.

After a few days of rest, New York will be back in action Saturday night when they take on the Cleveland Cavaliers. Tip off is scheduled for 8 p.m.

The Washington Wizards are integrating a few new pieces into the team, which explains why there are going to be growing pains for this squad. #2728. Recap: Wizards plagued by familiar issues in 120-105 loss to Hawks

The Washington Wizards' 120-105 loss to the Atlanta Hawks at Capital One Arena on Wednesday followed a script similar to the team's first three defeats this season. The home team was outshot from long range and gave up far too many offensive rebounds.

Anthony Davis got off to a hot start, scoring 6 of the Wizards' first 8 points. He tweaked his ankle just over a minute into the contest after landing on AJ Dybantsa's foot on a closeout. But Davis still finished with 10 points through the first 12 minutes.

Despite Washington seemingly playing well, Atlanta stayed ahead with the three-ball. The Hawks hit 8 three-pointers in the first quarter alone to take a 37-32 lead after one.

Dybantsa had a tough night offensively. He looked out of control at times and failed to get a veteran whistle on some of his drives. He took his frustrations out on the rim with a two-handed jam in the second quarter.

A triple from old friend CJ McCollum gave the Hawks a 16-point lead with 2:13 to play. The Wizards closed the half on a 9-0 run to cut the deficit to 68-61 at the half. Davis led all scorers with 18 points, along with 6 rebounds and 2 blocks at the break.

Kyshawn George ran point whenever Young was off the floor. He evidently picked up a few things from the All-Star point guard, as he repeatedly found Davis and Deandre Ayton for easy baskets around the rim.

The defense was much improved in the third quarter, but it was the offense lagged behind. Washington finally built up some momentum late when Trae hit a step-back three that got the team within four points of Atlanta.

Will Riley missed a clean look at a three on the following possession that would have gotten the Wizards to within one. The Hawks made it hurt as another old friend, Corey Kispert, connected on a four-point play on the other end.

George had a huge fourth quarter. He came alive with 12 points in the period but did not have much support from his Wizards teammates as the Hawks pulled away for the 15-point victory.

The Hawks more than tripled (19) the Wizards (6) in three-point makes. Atlanta already had Washington's three-point total midway through the first quarter. The Wizards also gave up 19 offensive rebounds as Dyson Daniels and Onyeka Okongwu combined to grab 33 boards.

Davis powered through his ankle injury to tally 26 points and 10 rebounds. George flashed more of his star potential with 25 points on 10-of-14 shooting, on top of his 7 assists.

Dybantsa and Tre Johnson both struggled from the field in this one. The No. 1 overall pick had his first poor outing offensively, with 9 points on a 4-of-12 clip. He also badly missed on 3 of his 4 free-throw attempts. Johnson looked rattled after his first few misses. He continued to force his shots through garbage time, making just 1 of his 9 attempts.

The Wizards get an immediate chance to avenge the loss when they head to Atlanta to face the Hawks on Friday for their second NBA Cup game.

#2726. No. 11 Maryland men’s soccer claims crucial 2-0 victory over Penn State to end the regular season

Despite being highly-ranked, No. 11 Maryland men's soccer found itself in fifth place in the Big Ten conference, looking to clinch a postseason berth with a win over Penn State – a team it had failed to defeat for years. Prior to Wednesday's match, the majority of the Terps' games this season had been decided by slim margins that prevented it from becoming consistent and comfortable.

Coming back home to Ludwig Field following a narrow road loss to No. 7 Washington on Friday, Maryland was able to secure a regular-season finale victory over Penn State with a final score of 2-0. That marked its first victory over Penn State since 2018 and its first victory by multiple goals this season.

While the Nittany Lions arrived in College Park riding momentum, having defeated Duquesne 3-1 on Oct. 28, they had nothing left to lose. Penn State was bottom of the conference standings with a record of 0-6-3 beforeWednesday's fixture.

Maryland made it clear it was looking to score and score fast in the first half. Within the first few minutes of the game, Maryland fired multiple shots on Penn State goalkeeper Justin Ross.

Relentlessly, Maryland's attack pressed on, creating an opportunity for Maryland's assist leader Henry Bernstein to pass the ball to Rodrigo Neri. The forward then found captain Albi Ndrenika, who buried a low-center goal in the seventh minute of play for his fourth score of the season.

Ndrenika's goal served as a wake-up call for the Nittany Lions, who began attacking Maryland's defense more fiercely. Regardless, Maryland showed its strength on both sides of the pitch, shutting down Penn State's playmakers before they could find their best goalscorers. It wasn't until the 19th minute that Penn State recorded its first shot on goal; that was routinely saved by Maryland goalkeeper Laurin Mack.

Penn State forward Etienne Reck made a run following a goal kick by Ross that gave him space to shoot inside Maryland's box. However, Maryland's defense blocked Reck's shot, preventing Penn State from finding its equalizer.

In the 33rd minute, Penn State delivered a corner kick that nearly resulted in a close-range goal. However, Mack instinctively dove to make the save.

Following his save, Mack initiated a counterattack, sending the ball to the left wing where Henry Bernstein delivered a cross to Dominic Ayella. But with quick reflexes, Ross stopped the thunderous shot.

The Terps continued to play with fierce intensity. The game became more physical, with the teams recording a combined 12 fouls as the first half began to wind down. With less than 30 seconds left on the clock, Ayella played a through ball for Marco Wright, who narrowly missed high, keeping the score at 1-0 to end the first half.

Coming out of halftime, Maryland continued to apply strong offensive pressure, forcing Ross to make demanding saves. Similarly, Penn State spent its first second-half trying to force its way through Maryland's defense with ball movement.

The Terps remained a threat. With one simple counterattack in the 54th minute, Maryland forward Rocket Ritarita delivered a pinpoint shot to the bottom right corner that Ross just managed to get his hand to, keeping the Nittany Lions at a one goal deficit.

Three minutes later, defender Lillian Fichelle found midfielder Zack Harris, who delivered a far-corner cross from outside the box to Ayella. His strong, bouncing header found the back of the net, doubling Maryland's lead.

Despite being close with each other on the stat sheet, Maryland firmly held its lead. But disaster struck for Maryland in the 74th minute when Ljubomir Popovic committed a foul as the last defender on a Penn State attack, resulting in a red card for the Maryland defender.

Penn State was at a clear advantage after Maryland's rejection, and because of that, it began attempting to overload the Terps' defense. But even a man down, the Terps managed to hold off the Nittany Lions to the very end, clinching a Big Ten tournament berth.

1. The offense dominated. In Wednesday's matchup, Maryland recorded 18 shots — with nine on frame — and capitalized on defensive errors that allowed it to take control of the game.

2. Popovic's suspension could be concerning. The defender has been crucial to Maryland's success, finding the goal on 40% of his shots and recording six assists in the season for the Terps. His red card suspension could create an opportunity for other teams to exploit moving forward.

3. Momentum going into the Big Ten tournament. Following the win from Wednesday's match, Maryland now looks to carry its momentum into a challenging postseason.

"We know how deep we have to dig," Ndrenika said. "…It's matured a lot of our guys, and they know how hard it's gonna be, and, yeah, we're ready for it."

#2725. Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert respond to Quentin Lake's "seeing ghosts" critique

As the football-following world tries to figure out the problem(s) with Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, Rams safety Quentin Lake provided a scathing critique of Herbert's most recent performance, in a 24-9 loss to the Rams.

"He was throwing deli meat out there," Lake said. "He's seeing ghosts. I don't know what's going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one."

On Wednesday, both Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake's remarks.

"As far as anybody's opinion I don't see that," Harbaugh told reporters. "Everybody's entitled to their opinion. Not what I see."

So what did Harbaugh see in the latest loss?

"I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well," Harbaugh said. "You know, two throws he would have liked to have back."

Herbert said he wasn't aware of Lake's comments.

"I haven't looked into it, haven't heard anything about it, so I can't really make a comment about it," Herbert told reporters. "We're really just focused on what's going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that's all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control."

Still, it's jarring to hear an NFL defender make comments about a supposed franchise quarterback that make him seem like a Jets first-round draft pick who has yet to have the game slow down. Herbert is in the seventh year of his career. He's making $52.5 million per year.

Something has happened this year. It's still not clear what it is, or whether it will change. Before it can change, the Chargers need to realize there's a problem.

And that's the most confounding part of all of it. They've lost seven and won none; at times, they sound like they've won seven and lost none.

#2723. What happened to Kon Knueppel? Hornets star's season debut ends after 6 minutes

The Charlotte Hornets were eagerly awaiting the regular season debut of second-year star and Rookie of the Year runner-up Kon Knueppel.

The Hornets ruled Knueppel out for the remainder of their game Wednesday, Nov. 4 against the Brooklyn Nets with left leg soreness. This is particularly concerning because Knueppel had been sidelined with a left hamstring strain.

After the game, Hornets coach Charles Lee told the local broadcast that he did not have an update on Knueppel and said he would be evaluated once the team returned to Charlotte later Wednesday.

Although there didn't appear to be a specific play in which Knueppel got hurt, he exited shortly after he dribbled the ball off his foot. During the play, Knueppel tried to dribble the ball behind his back but it caromed off his right leg, forcing him to take a small step as he tried to recover it. Immediately after the play, Knueppel limped but tried to stay in the game before quickly heading to the bench. He eventually went into the locker room and did not return.

Knueppel scored 3 points, all from free throws, missed his only shot attempt, a 3-pointer, and committed 2 turnovers in 5:51 on the floor against the Nets. He did not record any other statistic.

"Hopefully I can contribute in a capacity similar to last year, and with all the offseason work that I put in, even more," Knueppel told the Hornets broadcast in a pregame interview. "It might take me a little bit to get to that full capability, but tonight I'll be ready to go and help us get a win."

Last season, his first in the NBA after the Hornets selected him with the No. 4 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, Knueppel recorded 18.5 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. He converted 3-pointers at a 42.5% clip and lost out to his college teammate at Duke, Cooper Flagg, for the Rookie of the Year honor.

#2722. 2026 NHL free agent tracker: Patrick Kane returns to Blackhawks on two-year contract

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

NHL free agency has slowed down in late July, but some notable names are still coming off the board. Most notably, Patrick Kane is returning to the Chicago Blackhawks on a two-year contract worth $16 million, the team announced on Thursday.

Already a Chicago legend and future Hall of Famer, Kane won three Stanley Cups and a slew of individual awards with the franchise that selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in 2007. Kane's first stint with the Blackhawks lasted 16 seasons, and he piled up 446 goals and 779 assists in 1,161 games. Kane ranks inside the top five of just about every statistical category in franchise history, and he will get the chance to keep climbing those lists over the next two years.

The Blackhawks sent Kane to the New York Rangers at the 2023 NHL trade deadline, and he played just 19 regular season games there before hitting free agency the next summer. Hip surgery delayed Kane's decision until November of that year, but he ultimately landed with the Detroit Red Wings, where he's spent the last three seasons.

Last season was Kane's best with Detroit, and it proved that he still had some gas left in the tank, at least offensively. Kane posted 16 goals and 41 assists in 67 games -- with 19 of those points coming on the power play.

In his second stint with the Blackhawks, Kane will add another level of playmaking to the power play, and he should strengthen a top six forward group that's bereft of proven talent. Kane will also be an excellent mentor and sounding board for fellow No. 1 overall pick, Connor Bedard, who is set to miss the first month of the season after undergoing shoulder surgery.

Kane isn't the player he once was, but he'll give Chicago a bit more pop at the top of the lineup, and his first game back in a Blackhawks jersey will be a huge night for the city.

#2718. Eagles-Commanders somehow breaks 19 million viewers

When George Costanza pitched the show about nothing to NBC president Russell Dalrymple, Dalrymple asked, “Well, why am I watching it?”

More than 30 years later, that sentiment still applies. As evidenced by the fact that, per Nielsen, 19.015 million (on average) watched Sunday night’s snoozefest between the Eagles and Commanders on the network that Dalrymple once ran.

It’s an amazing number, given that it was the 2-5 Eagles against the 1-4-1 Commanders. The game itself wasn’t particularly compelling, and it followed afternoon windows that culminated in a down-to-the-wire showdown between the Chiefs and the Broncos.

The league could have flexed the game out of the evening window. It chose not to. In the end, the not-ready-for-prime-time game managed to attract far more viewers than anyone would have expected.

It helped that there wasn’t a 9:30 a.m. ET game in Week 8. Fourteen straight hours of football is a lot, even for the most ardent fan.

Then again, Commanders-Eagles was a lot. Even for the most ardent fan. And more than 19 million nevertheless watched the game.

So, what will that journey look like? The Carolina Hurricanes are looking to defend their title as Cup champions, but they'll have to contend with a deep Eastern Conference and some real juggernauts in the Western Conference. We also called our shot on the winners of each major individual award. Connor McDavid is looking for his fourth Hart Trophy, but he's got some competition from an up-and-coming superstar in his own division. Races for the Norris Trophy and Vezina Trophy should be pretty wide open, and unexpected candidates always emerge throughout the season.

It should be a fun season in the NHL, so follow along with all our coverage at CBS Sports. Let's get things kicked off with the season preview and predictions, which will of course be 100% accurate.

Baumgartner: I don't see many new faces entering the conversation when it comes to the Eastern Conference playoff race. Nivison -- Columbus Blue Jackets: The Blue Jackets have been agonizingly close to the playoffs in each of the last two seasons, and I think they get over the hump in 2026-27. Internal improvements from the young core will then get Columbus above the cut line.

Baumgartner -- San Jose Sharks: The Sharks narrowly missed out on the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs, finishing just four points short of the second wild card. San Jose added a good group of veterans over the summer, but the most important offseason move was selecting Ivar Stenberg with the No. 2 pick in the Draft. Stenberg joins the youth movement in San Jose, which is spearheaded by new captain Macklin Celebrini, who broke the Sharks single-season points record with 115 last season. Nivison: Yes, the Mammoth have a brutal path coming out of the Central Divison, but just close your eyes and imagine this scenario with me. Logan Cooley becomes a superstar center. Baumgartner: Before last season, the Carolina Hurricanes' kryptonite was the Eastern Conference Final. In the West, the Dallas Stars have been running into the same problem. With just two years left on his current contract, desperation may start to kick in to get the job in Edmonton, which would lead to another MVP-caliber season. #2716. The Daniel Jones Hate Is Just A Bit Out of Control

Hear me out, because I know even the thought of this article is going to upset a lot of people.

Daniel Jones has not played good football. I realize that. When you're the quarterback of an NFL franchise, especially on a new contract, you're paid to deliver. It's November, and the only thing he's delivered is a firesale.

I'm not naive about how bad he's been. He has 9 INTs and 2 wins, ranks 32nd in passer rating, has the second-worst TD-to-INT ratio and EPA/dropback in the league, and sits 25th in completion percentage.

But I truly believe quarterbacks get too much praise when things go well and too much blame when they don't. I'm not absolving Jones of his play, but proper criticism requires proper context, and a lot of the criticism he's getting has none.

Let's start with how the Colts built this roster in the first place.

The idea behind Jones' play last year was that he was in a better ecosystem than he had in New York. Then the Colts paid him and put him out there with ten other guys who now look a lot like what he had with the Giants. Why are we so surprised?

Heading into the year, the Colts were essentially running it back on offense, swapping out Pittman and Braden Smith for Keenan Allen and Jalen Travis. Shouldn't be too bad, right? Well, it has been.

Without AD Mitchell, there was no depth on the roster, and the Alec Pierce injury proved devastating. Josh Downs was supposed to soften the blow by playing more in heavier personnel looks. Obviously, that hasn't worked out.

Not to make this about Downs, but when you give up on highly talented WRs, do a lackluster job replenishing the room, and bet on guys to take on expanded roles they probably were never suited for, this is what happens.

Base to 11 is a major part of what's plaguing the Colts at the moment. What is Base to 11? When the Colts come out in three WR sets or 11 personnel, defenses are leaving their base defense on the field.

Why would they do that? They don't respect the speed of the offense. Why bring out more corners if you know none of these WRs are going to run by you. We can just leave bigger bodies and sell out vs. the run, because if they pass, we'll be just fine.

The Colts are battling some very complex looks that the personnel deficiencies make it impossible to overcome. Every defenses is compressed. Safeties are playing top down and nailing down on anything underneath.

In my opinion, this is the issue with the Colts right now.

They cannot pass out of these looks. They don't have enough speed on the field.

Base-to-11 and aggressive coverage techniques are one thing, but they also are consistently shooting themselves in the foot.

They are averaging 7.5 penalties a game in the last two weeks, back-to-back weeks of holding penalties negating large kickoffs and leading to backed up scenarios, missed field goals, dropped passes that turn into pick 6's.. the list really goes on.

The Colts have a laundry list of problems and the biggest indictment on Daniel Jones is that he hasn't been the solution.

He is a guy who is fighting off an Achilles issue, playing behind an offense that can't stretch a defense, and asked to carry a roster that has failed to support him at every turn.

The Colts needed a quarterback who could elevate the entire roster, and I mean elevate it to a level most teams have reached in the last five years… the postseason.

But has Daniel Jones ever been that kind QB? No. We just saw that in New York.

So why did the Colts pay him just to ask him to elevate a bad WR room, while he's coming off an achilles injury. It just doesn't make sense.

Not to mention the defense has been one of the worst in the league, if they were even league average the Daniel Jones discourse wouldn't be as loud, because the Colts would likely have more than just 2 wins.

Week after week we see defenses sell out to stop the run while Daniel Jones tries to pass his way behind the sticks in environments that aren't optimized for a QB like him to be successful.

So yes, Daniel Jones has not played good football. But if you're going to hate him for the way he's played, hate the front office first. Because I think Daniel Jones can play a lot better than he has, and maybe if he's traded he'll get a chance to show that again.

#2707. Jim Harbaugh, Justin Herbert respond to Quentin Lake's "seeing ghosts" critique

As the football-following world tries to figure out the problem(s) with Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert, Rams safety Quentin Lake provided a scathing critique of Herbert’s most recent performance, in a 24-9 loss to the Rams.

“He was throwing deli meat out there,” Lake said. “He’s seeing ghosts. I don’t know what’s going on, but we knew we were gonna get a couple. At least one.”

On Wednesday, both Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh and Herbert himself were asked about Lake’s remarks.

“As far as anybody’s opinion I don’t see that,” Harbaugh told reporters. “Everybody’s entitled to their opinion. Not what I see.”

So what did Harbaugh see in the latest loss?

“I thought he played — did his job exceptionally well,” Harbaugh said. “You know, two throws he would have liked to have back.”

Herbert said he wasn’t aware of Lake’s comments.

“I haven’t looked into it, haven’t heard anything about it, so I can’t really make a comment about it,” Herbert told reporters. “We’re really just focused on what’s going on in the building, playing football and doing what we can and doing our best to, you know, go put our best effort out on Sunday. And that’s all that really matters. Anything outside of that is out of our control.”

Still, it’s jarring to hear an NFL defender make comments about a supposed franchise quarterback that make him seem like a Jets first-round draft pick who has yet to have the game slow down. Herbert is in the seventh year of his career. He’s making $52.5 million per year.

Something has happened this year. It’s still not clear what it is, or whether it will change. Before it can change, the Chargers need to realize there’s a problem.

And that’s the most confounding part of all of it. They’ve lost seven and won none; at times, they sound like they’ve won seven and lost none.

#2705. Soccer-Referee hands out record 53 red cards after mass brawl erupts in Brazilian under-20s match

Nov 5 (Reuters) - An under-20s match in the Brazilian state of Minas Gerais descended into complete chaos, with the referee having to hand out a record ‌53 red cards following a massive brawl.

The brawl took place during the first ‌leg of a state championship semifinal match between Uberlandia and Mamore on Sunday.

In his report of the match, referee ​Fernando Patrick Drosghic Modesto said the trouble began early in the second half, when a number of Uberlandia officials invaded the field of play after one of their players was sent off.

The match was halted for 40 minutes and eventually restarted, with Mamore going on to score in ‌the ninth minute of stoppage time ⁠to take a 3-1 lead.

According to reports in Brazilian media, Mamore player Davi taunted Uberlandia players during the goal celebrations, which sparked a massive ⁠brawl and led to a deluge of red cards.

A total of 43 players and 8 members of the coaching staff were sent off, while 2 Uberlandia board members were also dismissed, taking ​the tally ​up to 53.

"In the 54th minute of the ​second half, a generalized brawl broke ‌out, making it impossible to show the red cards and to carry out the match-closing protocol," Drosghic Modesto wrote in his report.

"Therefore, owing to all the turmoil and the lack of security, I declared the match ended."

Drosghic Modesto added that a police report had been filed over threats made against the referee and that Mamore's team had vandalised the dressing room after ‌the match.

The previous Guinness World Record for the most ​red cards shown in a match was 36, which ​occurred in February 2011 during a ​fifth-division match in Argentina between Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas.

On Wednesday, Uberlandia ‌said it would be forfeiting the second ​leg of the semifinal ​in a "gesture of fair play," since Mamore did not have enough eligible players to field a team.

The forfeit saw Mamore qualify for the final of the tournament.

"The club ​has also not remained silent: ‌the appropriate disciplinary measures regarding those involved have already been taken internally, because ​athletic development is, above all, a matter of personal development," Uberlandia added.

(Reporting by ​Aadi Nair in Bengaluru; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus)

#2700. Josh Jacobs: "There's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false"

On Friday, Wisconsin authorities released documents in the Josh Jacobs criminal case that included three allegations against him from other women. On Wednesday, Jacobs spoke directly to reporters for the first time since the material became public.

“It’s one of those things for me where it’s like, it really feels like an attack on me and who I am and my character,” Jacobs said, via Rob Demovsky of ESPN. “And at the end of the day, there’s a lot of stuff being said about me that’s completely false -- like, completely made up, and it’s like people just run with it. And I can’t change that.

“It’s just one of those things where it’s like, OK, all I can do is try to be who I am and try not to let the negative moments change who I am. And that was the biggest thing for me throughout this whole process. I didn’t want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I’m angry all the time because of what’s going on in my life.”

The situation would be very different if Jacobs hadn’t pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor battery charge arising from an incident in May 2026. Admitting to an incident of violence against a woman makes it harder for him to credibly claim that three other women who contacted authorities about Jacobs doing the same thing are making it all up.

Still, Jacobs believes the newly-surfaced allegations won’t result in more missed time, following the six-game stint on paid leave arising from the most recent incident.

“With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it’s not one of those things where I’m sitting back on my hands like, ‘OK, am I going to play this week?’” Jacobs said. “It’s like, I kind of already know what it is, so it’s like . . . it’s really just up to them to make their final decision. But like I’m not worried about feeling like I’m going to miss any more time than I already have.”

The league continues to investigate Jacobs, and it’s investigating the recent allegations, too. Through it all, the Packers have been linked on multiple occasions to a potential trade for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. If the Packers land Taylor, it could mean that they’ll move on from Jacobs.

#2698. Report: Jalen Hurts makes an appearance at team facility

Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts made an appearance at the team’s practice facility on Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN reports.

It is the first time some players had seen Hurts since he went on injured reserve with blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts sat in on the team meeting and additional meetings, but he did not address the team.

Coach Nick Sirianni did not address a question Wednesday about whether the quarterback had been at the facility.

“I’ve talked to him and am in constant communication with him and know he’s resting and recovering,” Sirianni said. “I miss him like crazy. But nothing new on that front. I know he’s resting and recovering, and we’re all still praying for him and hoping for a speedy recovery.”

Hurts, 28, went on injured reserve on Oct. 17 and is expected to miss the rest of the season.

Tanner McKee went 0-3 in Hurts’ absence before being benched for Joe Milton this week.

#2697. Everything to know for Bengals vs. Falcons in Madrid

The Cincinnati Bengals are in Madrid to face the Atlanta Falcons in NFL Week 9. The game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. on Nov. 8 and the game will be broadcast locally on NBC/WLWT-TV and nationally on NFL Network.

Cincinnati (5-2) is coming off a win over the Tennessee Titans and Atlanta (3-5) is coming off a loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

The Bengals will meet with the media today as head coach Zac Taylor will host a press conference for media in Madrid and players also will be available for interviews.

Here's what you need to know for the week:

The Bengals are practicing on Nov. 5 and 6. The team will not have media availability on Nov. 7. The Bengals vs. Falcons Week 9 game is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. Eastern on Nov. 8.

The Bengals traveled to Madrid on Nov. 3 and will fly back home after the game on Nov. 8. Cincinnati will host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 15 at Paycor Stadium on "Sunday Night Football."

Madrid is located in the Central European Time zone, which is six hours ahead of the Eastern Time zone. The Week 9 game between the Bengals and Falcons will take place at 3:30 p.m. locally in Madrid, which is 9:30 a.m. Eastern.

The Bengals are 0-1-1 in two international games. Both games were played at Wembley Stadium in London.

The first time the Bengals played overseas was in 2016 against the Washington Commanders. The game ended in a 27-27 tie. The last time the Bengals were overseas was Zac Taylor's first season as head coach and Cincinnati lost 24-10 to the Los Angeles Rams. The Bengals would eventually meet the Rams in Super Bowl 56, suffering a 23-20 loss.

The Falcons have played one more game than the Bengals abroad and have a win as well. Atlanta's first game was a 21-20 loss to the Detroit Lions at Wembley Stadium in 2014, which was followed by a 27-20 win over the New York Jets at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London in 2021. The Falcons most recently had a 23-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2023.

The Bengals lead the all-time series against the Falcons at 10-5. The two teams most recently met Oct. 23, 2022 at Paycor Stadium and the Bengals won 35-17. The 2022 win made it a three-game winning streak for the Bengals against the Falcons.

#2696. Alexander Ovechkin announces this will be his last NHL season: 'Let's have fun'

If not listed, please contact your TV provider.

Alex Ovechkin's 22nd NHL season will be his last, the Washington Capitals superstar announced on Monday."This is gonna be my last year," Ovechkin told his teammates in a video the Capitals posted to social media. "It's sad, but it is what it is. We have an unbelievable team this year. There are 82 games left. Let's make the playoffs, and let's have fun."

Ovechkin has already established himself as the greatest goal-scorer in hockey history with 929 tallies, and he still has 82 games to add to that total before he hangs up his skates.

The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NHL Draft, Ovechkin immediately established himself as a prolific scorer by notching 52 goals en route to winning the Calder Trophy as a rookie.

Since then, Ovechkin has won the Rocket Richard Trophy as the NHL's leading goal-scorer a record nine times. The Capitals legend's resume also features an Art Ross Trophy and three Hart Trophy wins.

The crowning achievement in Ovechkin's illustrious career is leading Washington to its first Stanley Cup in 2017-18. After coming up short in a number of postseasons prior to that, Ovechkin led all playoff performers with 15 goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy as a result.

Following the 2025-26 season, there was speculation that Ovechkin could retire, but he signed an incentive-laden one-year deal with the Caps.Sensing that this could be Ovechkin's final season, the Capitals loaded up to give their franchise icon one more shot at the Stanley Cup. Washington signed former Buffalo Sabres winger Alex Tuch in free agency and acquired winger Jordan Kyrou from the St. Louis Blues via trade.

No team is as loaded on the wings as the Capitals, and they have one of the best rosters in the Metro Division. Washington has the ingredients to challenge the defending Cup champion Carolina Hurricanes and get Ovechkin one more ring before he rides off into the sunset.

#2695. Player Grades: Cavs at Thunder: Donovan Mitchell’s fourth-quarter outing not enough

The Cleveland Cavaliers falter for the second time against an injury-riddled Oklahoma City Thunder team, falling 124-116

Grades are based on our usual expectations for each player.

19 points, 6 assists, 9 rebounds, 2 blocks

The Cavaliers would have had no pulse in their contest with the Thunder if not for Harden. It felt like even when the Cavs were down by double digits in the second and third quarter that Harden was the only one really trying to assemble an offense.

Harden might not have been the most efficient player on the floor. He was, however, the true spark keeping the Cavaliers within arm's reach. In a loss where the bulk of the team was struggling to match the Thunder's energy on the floor, Harden met the task.

16 points, 10 rebounds, 3 assists, 3 blocks

Without Jarrett Allen for most of the game, you would have figured that Mobley would become an even bigger focus on offense. However, Mobley was not up to the task tonight. If Mobley did not have an open lane, it felt like he would vanish on offense.

While he ended up putting up a respectable stat line, those who watched the game would note how invisible he felt at times.

27 points, 3 assists, 5 rebounds, 2 turnovers

It is strange to put a player who scored the bulk of the team's fourth-quarter points not as the player of the game; however, it felt like it took until the last few minutes of the game for Mitchell to emerge as even a factor in the contest.

Mitchell put on an absolute clinic in the last five minutes, scoring 17 of his 27 points to get the Cavaliers back within single digits. While appreciated to try and lead one last push, it felt like if this type of aggression was there earlier on the Cavaliers wouldn't have faced such a tough deficit to overcome.

This was arguably the most disappointing outing for the young rookie. Thomas was able to put the ball in the hoop, however, this felt like the most desperate shot volume of his young career.

The shots seemed rushed, or even like Thomas was trying to shoot himself into a groove. Games like this happen, and Thomas was still a shot of energy in the lineups he was placed into.

Jarrett was essentially a non-factor in this contest as he suffered a lower leg injury. This injury took place when he went knee-to-knee during a standard pick. Allen was able to walk off the floor under his own power. Head coach Kenny Atkinson didn't have an update on the severity of the injury post-game.

Hezonja was one of the few players who were providing a spark for the Cavaliers against the Thunder. His perimeter defense and being engaged off-ball allowed him to score 12 points in a variety of ways. As Hezonja continues to put up quality minutes, one would hope this would allow him to see minutes with the core four.

On a night where Merrill didn't go nuclear from the arc, this was probably the closest you would get to a good outing from the sharpshooter. He was an active presence on the glass, keeping his value on the floor going even if the elite volume and percentage were not there tonight.

Proctor got the starting nod tonight with Jaylon Tyson and Peyton Watson out and was…fine? Proctor shot the ball well enough, he just was not dynamic enough otherwise to feel like additive to the starting five. It's nice not to worry about whether his shots will fall, but there is not much else to really gain for Proctor in the starting lineup.

This could be a me problem. I really did not enjoy my Thomas Bryant experience tonight. It felt like the bulk of his possessions were him hoisting up shots from beyond the arc.

They are tolerable when they fall. When they don't, they feel like the most painful offensive possessions the Cavaliers can muster.

Enaruna got some serious run tonight and put up mixed results on the floor. It felt like a break-glass-in-case-of-emergency type of nomination, and there certainly were growing pains in the outing. Enaruna flashed some good on-the-ball decision-making while also being composed with the ball in his hands.

Where Enaruna struggled was from the perimeter. Never seen so many in-and-out threes in one game as he had tonight.

#2694. AFC North Week 8 Recap: Steelers take the lead; Ravens lose Lamar Jackson

Week 8 had major ramifications for the AFC North after Lamar Jackson suffered a potentially season-ending injury.

The Pittsburgh Steelers sit atop the division now at 6-2 after a 27-6 win over the Cleveland Browns.

Pittsburgh dominated Cleveland on both sides of the ball on Sunday. The offense rushed for 200 yards and three touchdowns while the defense sacked Deshaun Watson eight times and recovered two fumbles. Aaron Rodgers finished the game 13 of 25 for 172 yards and an interception. Jaylen Warren's big season continued with 143 rushing yards on 17 carries while Darnell Washington led all pass catchers with 94 yards on three catches.

Patrick Queen led the defense with 12 total tackles while also racking up 1.5 sacks and a pass defense. Keeanu Benton and Daylen Everette both recovered fumbles.

The Cincinnati Bengals outlasted the Tennessee Titans in a 43-36 shootout to improve to 5-2.

Joe Burrow's three interceptions on the day were offset by his five touchdown passes. He finished the game 38 of 48 for 462 yards. Tee Higgins was once again Burrow's top target, catching 10 passes for 155 yards and a pair of touchdowns. Ja'Marr Chase had a monster day as well, with 141 yards and a touchdown on 11 catches. Chase Brown led the rushing attack with 55 yards on 12 carries while also losing a fumble.

The Bengals allowed Cam Ward to throw for 304 yards and two touchdowns while also giving up 158 yards and two touchdowns on the ground. Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe each had a sack on Ward, while Lawrence and Josh Newton both recovered fumbles.

The Browns ceded the division lead with a 27-6 loss to the Steelers.

Deshaun Watson was placed in the concussion protocol on Tuesday following a game in which he was sacked eight times. Watson finished the game on Sunday with 27 completions on 39 attempts for 324 yards. The ground game was a non-factor for Cleveland as the offense racked up just 34 rushing yards on 15 carries. Harold Fannin Jr.'s 154 receiving yards on 10 catches led the team. Both Watson and Fannin lost fumbles.

Jared Verse has yet to record a sack since joining the Browns as part of the Myles Garrett trade. Verse's lack of impact was especially notable on Sunday after he spent the week trash-talking Pittsburgh. Adin Huntingon recorded Cleveland's lone sack while Carson Schwesinger led the defense with 10 total tackles.

The Baltimore Ravens dropped their third game in a row with a 36-10 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

The biggest loss of the day for the Ravens, however, was undoubtedly at quarterback, as Lamar Jackson lasted just one play in his return from an ankle injury. On the play, Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could potentially end his season. Tyler Huntley then suffered a season-ending toe injury in replacement for Jackson, leading to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finishing the game under center. The three quarterbacks combined for less than 100 passing yards, an interception, and two lost fumbles. A trade for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett has since been announced and is expected to be finalized after Baltimore's Thursday night game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Zay Flowers was completely blanked, catching zero of his five targets. Rashod Bateman's 22 receiving yards led the team, while Derrick Henry totaled 53 rushing yards and a touchdown on 11 carries.

The Ravens' defense held on for as long as they could reasonably be expected to, with little help from their offense. Roquan Smith had one of the best games of his season with 11 total tackles to go with two pass deflections and a forced fumble. Nnamdi Madubuike and Mike Green split the defense's only sack on Josh Allen.

#2693. Matthew Stafford has full participation with elbow injury; Myles Garrett limited in return

Rams coach Sean McVay wouldn’t allow much about the ice pack on quarterback Matthew Stafford’s arm after Sunday’s win over the Chargers other than to say it was soreness. The injury report said it isn’t serious, and Stafford agreed.

Stafford was a full participant, listed with an elbow injury.

“I’m 38 years old, trying to keep up with these young bucks. Little bit of soreness and stuff that is not uncommon this time of year,” Stafford said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times. “Haven’t missed a rep. Feel good. So I’m not too worried about it.”

Stafford underwent surgery on his elbow during the 2022 offseason.

The Rams got more good news when outside linebacker Myles Garrett (knee) returned to practice as a limited participant. It was the first practice Garrett and Aaron Donald have had together.

Garrett underwent arthroscopic knee surgery in mid-September after playing 40 snaps in the season opener. He was given a six-week prognosis and has missed seven games.

The Rams practiced without cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back), tight end Colby Parkinson (ribs) and safety Kam Curl (foot) on Wednesday.

Inside linebacker Grant Stuard (hamstring), offensive lineman Steve Avila (hamstring), wide receiver Jordan Whittington (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle) were limited.

#2690. Nick Bosa returns to practice with limited work

49ers defensive end Nick Bosa returned to practice Wednesday after missing the team’s past five games with a calf injury. Bosa was a limited participant.

“It’s a long year, and I kind of just reminded myself that I need to be ready for the long haul,” Bosa said, via Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle.

Bosa tore his right ACL in a Sept. 21, 2025, game against the Cardinals and underwent surgery five days later. As he was coming back this summer, Bosa experienced soreness and tendinitis in his right knee, and the 49ers backed him down until Sept. 2 when he returned to practice.

He injured his left calf while warming up in practice for Week 3.

“I must have had some type of compensation going on, especially in that first week back,” Bosa said. “I was kind of trying to push it back with the [right knee] tendinitis, so I may have been favoring [the left calf] a little bit. I was just doing my normal warm-up drills one day, and I tweaked it. Calves are a pretty long process. I’ve never had one, so it took a little longer than I expected, but I don’t even think about it anymore.”

Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) remained out of practice, and running back Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) also didn’t practice.

#2688. Knicks' Jalen Brunson finds his groove in win over Bulls

So far this season, Knicks star point guard Jalen Brunson hasn't looked like the MVP-caliber player fans saw in the NBA Finals this past summer.

But one week after helping New York erase a 19-point deficit in Chicago, Brunson seemingly officially found his groove Wednesday night against the Bulls. However, instead of showing up as basketball's best closer as he so often does, he hit the ground running early, racking up 22 points in 12-straight first-frame minutes and outscoring the entire Bulls roster by one.

He played just 17 more minutes across the remaining three quarters of the game but continued to find his way to the basket, increasing his total to a season-best 33 points. No other player tallied more than 18 (Karl-Anthony Towns). He hit five of his 10 three-point attempts, eight of his nine foul shots, and 10 of his 17 from the field.

"It's part of the game," he said of his effort. "Obviously, when you have it going, it feels good. Just trying to play off that and use your gravity to make plays."

Odds are, the reigning NBA Finals MVP would have kept scoring had he been given more time on the floor. At the rate he was going, he may have hit 80 points.

"Our analytics guys [chart] how guys play in two-minute increments," head coach Mike Brown explained after the game. "Some guys, after six minutes, their three-point field-goal percentage drops. They also can track their movement — how quickly they're still moving out on the floor, if that slows down or not. Jalen's just seems to go up every two minutes."

But Brown said his desire to protect Brunson's health significantly outweighs his curiosity regarding just how much Brunson could produce if he were left unrestrained. In fact, he said, keeping Brunson in the game just for the sake of it never even crossed his mind.

"He's about as durable as anybody I've been around. He's mentally tough, physically tough, and he can push himself to go," Brown said. "... But at the end of the day, it's going to impact him, in my opinion, come playoff time, so I have to be conscious of not going to the well too much, especially at this point in the season."

When asked if he would ever request to keep playing in a game like tonight, Brunson was hesitant.

"Possibly, but it has to be the right moment, right time," he said. "I don't want to say no because you never know when you're in this situation, but I just want to respect the game as much as possible."

As the Seattle Seahawks prepare for a pivotal NFC West contest with the Arizona Cardinals, they'll face a boatload of injuries, according to Wednesday's estimated injury report.

The Seahawks had six players miss practice with injury, including quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and star defensive tackle Leonard Williams. "Big Cat" was held out with a stinger he suffered on Monday night against the Chicago Bears and would be a massive loss for the team, especially in the run game. Nose tackle Brandon Pili also did not practice with a back injury, leaving Seattle thin at the position and facing a red-hot running back in Tyler Allgeier.

With Darnold out, Seahawks Mike Macdonald indicated that backup Drew Lock would start in his place. Lock has been battling an elbow injury for the last three weeks, was inactive in their last two games, and was once again limited in practice on Wednesday with a right elbow injury. If Lock can't go, second-year quarterback Jalen Milroe would need to step in to make his first NFL start, which would be as entertaining as it would be stressful.

Sticking with the offense, newly acquired star guard Quenton Nelson was limited by a knee injury, as was backup Anthony Bradford. With Josh Jones poised to start another week at left tackle, more offensive line injuries have to be the last thing Seahawks fans want to see.

The report proves to be a mixed bag for the Seahawks defense as well. Edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who missed last week, was limited with an ankle injury, and Nick Emmanwori was a full participant with a shoulder injury. Those two returning to form in the lineup would be a massive boost for the "Dark Side" defense that is reeling from giving up 34 points on Monday.

As for the Cardinals, breakout wide receiver Michael Wilson was limited in practice by rest and a rib injury, which could give him a chance to play on Sunday. Wilson broke two ribs and put up 111 yards and a touchdown on eight catches in Arizona's win over the Dallas Cowboys last week. Defensive tackle Walter Nolen was also limited with an ankle injury.

Arizona will likely be without running back Bam Knight, who would back up Allgeier, as he did not practice on Wednesday due to a concussion. The Cardinals held stars Budda Baker and Josh Sweat out of practice, but it was not injury-related.

Humorously, the Cardinals held quarterback Jacoby Brissett out with "rest," which apparently means getting shipped off to the Baltimore Ravens.
